notes:
An escort, and almost everything on the page is how to survive it rather than something you do at a place. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a cooldown -- one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet per Vana'dielian day across ALL of Abyssea -- which no packet reports. Bullet 4 is not a step: it is the outcome ('you will receive a message when the chocobo is close enough') plus the recommended path and the chocobo's panic behaviour, so it folds into step 3's note. Bullet 8 is the Bastion effect on Martello and Clone Ward HP, an outcome of finishing, not a rung.

The page names the destination twice and differently: bullet 3 sends you to the 'Repair Crate' at (G-7), bullet 5 tells you to click the 'large Repair Trunk'. Both fold cleanly in the normaliser, but nothing on the page says whether that is one object under two names or two objects at one spot. Both are recorded exactly where the page wrote them rather than reconciled -- whichever is the live entity will draw and the other simply never matches -- and the quest is demoted to medium for it.

The supplies are deliberately NOT modelled. Chocobo Blinkers, Stamina Apples, Azouph Greens and M. Counteragents are all real items and all resolve, but the page offers them as advice with a suggested minimum, they are BOUGHT at step 2 rather than held into it, and they are eaten during the escort -- evidence over them would read true at the shop and false again halfway to (G-7). The chocobo you click to load at step 4 is never named, so that half of bullet 5 has no target of its own and stays in the note. Fame 'aatt' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing; the FLevel of 1 is kept anyway. The wiki flags the whole page unverified.

steps.note: at Veridical Conflux #00. Only one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet quest can be completed per Vana'dielian day, in any Abyssea area.

the page gives no grid, only 'near the Resistance Sapper', so near (F-8). This is where you buy supplies and where the escort begins. Suggested: 6+ Chocobo Blinkers (traded to the bird, 90s, blinds it to monsters), 6 Stamina Apples (60s, slows its HP drain, does not stack with Blinkers), 6+ Azouph Greens (+5% HP, limited frequency), and a few M. Counteragents for the Miasma on the route. All advice, all consumed on the way, so none is recorded as an item or as evidence.

guide the chocobo the whole way avoiding every aggro; Silent Oil and Prism Powder on yourself still let it follow. Its HP drains the whole time, so be quick. If a monster gets line of sight on it, it says 'Kweh!?' and bolts back to the last safe spot -- run to it and interact to stop it. Recommended path: Stamina Apple immediately, north to the dead end, left and slightly north of the AT-04 Martello (Dark Miasma may be up), Silent Oil here or you will be ambushed, north hugging the right wall through the rocks, past the AT-06 Martello (Dark Miasma again), north staying in the rocks to the Inugami hounds, watch for the true-sight NM Gieremund, hug the wall into the tunnel. Bullet 3 calls the destination the Repair Crate; bullet 5 calls it the Repair Trunk -- see the quest note.

click the trunk to gather supplies, then click the chocobo to load them -- the bird is never named on the page, so that second click has no target of its own. Selecting Depart loads no more and moves the escort on. If you only want the completion, load one: more supplies slow the chocobo down, though a fuller bird restores more Bastion HP. Same name conflict with step 3.
retrace the route with the chocobo, then speak to the Tamer to end the escort
Cruor, Resistance Credits and possibly an Empyrean +1 head seal

notes:
Four bullets, all four on Yurim, so the entire quest is one marker on the top floor of Tavnazian Safehold and the ladder only records what you do there. The header's Start field is the bare name 'Yurim' with no zone at all; the zone and (J-8) come from bullet 1, which is where they should come from.

Bullet 5 is not a step. It is what completing the quest once UNLOCKS -- trading vices and auras from the Lumoria HNMs to Meret -- and Meret belongs to that other exchange, not to this ladder. The 'Related Links' section after the walkthrough is three wiki links and nothing else.

The substance of this quest is the table, and it cannot be expressed. Eighteen reward rows, each with its own base item plus chip and its own EX-item list, running from 5 Euvhi Organs up to 56 Phuabo Organs for all sixteen pieces. 'items' is an AND-list with a single 'items_alt' escape, not an eighteen-way switch, so steps 2 and 4 carry empty lists with items_partial set -- the honest 'there is an alternative I could not express at all' -- rather than one arbitrarily chosen row dressed up as the requirement.

No step carries evidence. The base item and chip are traded away at step 2, the EX organs are traded away at step 4, and the earring, obi or gorget you walk out with is the REWARD, which proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done. The optional Apple Pie trade in bullet 3 buys a hint the table already gives, on the same NPC in the same spot, so it is a note rather than a rung. ADVERSARY: 'Garden of Antiquity' has been REMOVED from gates.prev. It is named only in Quest Reqs; the header's Previous field is empty. Across the whole corpus prev is drawn from Previous and from nothing else, and Waking the Colossus has exactly this shape -- Previous empty, Quest Reqs 'Eternal Mercenary (Complete all ToAU Missions)' -- and carries prev []. The prerequisite is real; it is left unmodelled rather than promoted into a gate the header did not declare.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: Eighteen rows in the table and no way to say 'one of these eighteen pairs', so items_partial carries it.
  step 4: Same eighteen-way branch as step 2, so items_partial again.

steps.note: top floor. The header gives no zone for her; this is where it comes from.

Choose the reward FIRST, then trade its base item and its chip together Silver Earring, Silver Obi or Gorget with one of the eight coloured chips, or eight or sixteen of them at once for Hachirin-no-Obi or Fotia Gorget. The page warns you cannot cancel after choosing.

she names what to farm. You may instead trade her an Apple Pie for the same hint, which the page itself says is a waste next to the table -- an optional trade on the same NPC that changes nothing, so it is not a rung of its own.

The EX organs and tissue for the row you chose Aern, Hpemde, Phuabo, Xzomit, Euvhi and Yovra Organs and Luminian Tissue, in counts from 5 to 56 depending on the reward. The reward itself is not evidence.

notes:
Twenty-eight bullets, of which twenty-two are escort rules and route commentary. Bullets 5 to 15 are how Ken behaves -- what he engages, how many hits a lizard takes, how far he can see, that he snaps back onto his path and turns around into you -- and bullets 16 to 26 are the eight lines he speaks as he walks a fixed route, each with 'make sure you are out of sight' attached. Not one of them is something you do at a place, so they collapse into a single escort rung on Ken rather than twenty-two rungs the player can never be tracked through.

Bullet 2 is the dialogue choice ('I wasn't talking to you, squirt.') and belongs to bullet 1's conversation. The [TABLE] in the walkthrough renders empty because the wiki puts the route MAP there -- which is why bullets 16-26 read as captions to something that is not here. Nothing was lost that could have been a step.

The one observable thing in the quest is Ken's escort award, the key item Marin hands you at the Dangruf Wadi exit after Ken despawns, and it sits on that step and nowhere else. The two Marin steps are in DIFFERENT zones -- the exit inside Dangruf Wadi, then back in Bastok Markets -- so they are two markers rather than one, which is the whole reason the split is worth keeping. The level-10 cap in bullet 4 is imposed by the quest, not required to enter it, so it is not a level gate; the cap is lifted by the same conversation that grants the key item.

steps.note: when prompted you must pick "I wasn't talking to you, squirt." or the quest does not proceed
zoning in gives a short introductory cutscene. Arriving by Survival Guide does not count -- you must re-zone to get it.
this caps you at level 10 for the duration. Buffs already up stay up, but you cannot cast on Ken before starting.

the escort itself, twenty-two bullets of rules and route folded into one rung. You fail the instant Ken sees you, and his sight range is long; he engages everything in his line of sight, cannot be stopped like the three-nation escort NPCs, and is in trouble after three or four fights, so he needs curing without being spotted. He snaps back to his path after each kill, which usually turns him straight around into whoever was healing him. He walks a fixed route and announces his progress in eight lines: watching for a follower, getting lost, surveying, going further on, a dead end (hide behind the southern rock), the hot spring reading, another look behind him, and running circles in the first room. On the last line he heads for the zone line and despawns -- be BEHIND him for that, he faces outward and will see you.
she appears at the exit once Ken despawns; the page gives no grid for her there. This conversation both removes the level cap and grants the key item.

notes:
The walkthrough never mentions Esha'ntarl. Bullet 2 says only 'enter the palace in Ru'Lude Gardens', which is a place inside zone 243 rather than a zone of its own, and it names no entity at all -- so step 1 is a targetless rung and start stays on the header's Esha'ntarl. That is deliberately NOT the Carbuncle correction from the Summoner quests: there the header's giver was a cutscene and the House of the Hero was a real thing to move the marker TO, whereas here there is nothing to move it to, and Esha'ntarl is a genuine standing NPC who gives this whole Lay of the Immortals line. Leaving her as start keeps the pre-start marker exactly where a player needs it and invents no interaction the page does not describe.

Bullets 3, 4 and 5 each hold two things -- a zone entry, then something to click or someone to talk to inside it -- so each splits in two. The Al'Taieu leg between Sueleen and the Grand Palace of Hu'Xzoi is the ride she gives you, not a rung. Bullets 5 and 6 are the same object checked twice, first for a cutscene and then to open the battlefield, so they merge into one examine exactly as Divine Might's Blank Target does.

Everything in 'Boss Fight' bullets 1-4 and the whole ability table is tactics, but its bullets 5 and 6 are the last two steps of the quest -- Aldo, then Gilgamesh -- and without them the walkthrough ends inside a battlefield with no hand-in at all. Those two carry that section's own numbering, which restarts at [1]. Aldo is marked optional because the page gates his cutscene on Rank 5 or higher in your current nation, which nothing observable reports, and then says the completion timer is 'not tied to when you might have talked to Aldo'; a Rank 4 player finishes without him.

The 'Reacquisition' section is how to redo the quest for a different earring -- drop the old one, erase your memories at a ??? by the Empyreal Paradox entrance, redo this quest and the previous one -- not part of a single run of it. Two time gates the addon cannot see: a game day after Shadows of the Departed before this starts, and a Vana'diel day between the battlefield and Gilgamesh. No key items and nothing held anywhere, so no step carries evidence; the four earrings are the reward and prove only that it is over.

ADVERSARY: 'Zilart Mission 17' and 'Promathia Mission 8-4' have been REMOVED from gates.prev. Both come from Quest Reqs rather than the Previous field, and both are MISSIONS -- they cannot resolve against the quest tables, so as prev entries they are a gate that is never satisfied and would suppress the marker permanently. Only 'Shadows of the Departed', the actual Previous, remains; the two mission gates are left unmodelled, which is how A Thirst for Eternity handles the identical shape. Confidence dropped to medium: the walkthrough never names the quest giver at all, so start rests entirely on a header field the page never corroborates; step 1 is a rung with no target because the page names neither a door nor an NPC; and every gate that survives -- the two mission prerequisites, the Rank 5 condition on Aldo's cutscene, and the two game-day waits -- is unobservable. The ladder itself is unchanged and is believed correct.

steps.note: the page says only 'enter the palace', naming no door and no NPC, and the palace is inside Ru'Lude Gardens rather than a zone of its own -- so this rung deliberately has no target. You must also have zoned and waited until the next game day after finishing Shadows of the Departed.

zoning in gives the cutscene. If this is your first return since first visiting Al'Taieu you may get Sueleen's cutscene instead -- zone back to Tavnazian Safehold and re-enter for the correct one with Prishe.
she is the ride to Al'Taieu; the page gives no grid for her. The Al'Taieu leg itself is not a rung.
in from Al'Taieu

down from The Garden of Ru'Hmet. With the Lumoria > The Garden of Ru'Hmet > #1 home point, zone back out to the Grand Palace of Hu'Xzoi, warp in and descend. On Rune of Valor you may get a cutscene when you press Descend.
check it twice: the first is a cutscene, the second opens the battlefield

both brothers at once, originally uncapped at 75 and trivial at 99; Trusts are allowed. from the 'Boss Fight' section, whose bullets restart at [1] -- this is its bullet 5, not the walkthrough's. Marked optional: the cutscene needs Rank 5 or higher in your current nation, which is not observable, and the page says the completion timer is not tied to whether you talked to him.

also from the 'Boss Fight' section's own numbering -- its bullet 6. Zone and wait for the next Vana'diel day after clearing the battlefield first; that wait has counted from the battlefield, not from Aldo, since the November 2021 update.
